 Shri Devdeep Singh, learned counsel for the respondent   ORDER

This miscellaneous appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is preferred being aggrieved by the award dated 15.11.2018 in MACC No.71/15 by Member, MACT, Sarangpur, district Rajgarh challenging the liability of the appellant to pay the compensation to the claimant/respondent.

2. Facts in brief are that an application under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 was preferred seeking compensation of Rs.86 lakhs for the injuries caused in the motor vehicle accident dated 08.09.2010 when he was travelling in a mini truck bearing no.MP-09-GE-7725 carrying buffaloes.

3. The claim was contested by respondents No.1 & 2 submitting that the vehicle was insured with respondent no.3 and if any liability arises the same will be ordered to be satisfied by the insurance company.

4. The claim was contested by respondent No.3/appellant on various grounds including the breach of policy conditions to the effect that at the time of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:28904 2 MA-5654-2019 accident the vehicle was driven by the driver of the vehicle without valid and effective driving license, fitness and permit and further that the respondent No.1/claimant was taking the journey in the offending vehicle without goods

, therefore,
he is not entitled for any compensation.

sentences.text: 1 5. Tribunal framed issues and claimant examined himself as PW/1 and respondent No.2 Akbar Khan examined himself as DW/1 and appellant examined Pawan Kumar Agrawal as DW/2.

6. Appreciating the evidence of both the sides tribunal estimated the age of the claimant as 47 years,
his income as Rs.4000/- per month, permanent disability 10% and applying the multiplier of 13 calculated the loss of future income as Rs.62,400 and

after adding Rs.5,000/- as medical expenses,
Rs.20,000/- towards loss of income during treatment, Rs.5,000/- towards pain and suffering,
Rs.5000/- under the head of special diet and Rs.5000/- for grievous injuries awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,02,400/- with interest at the rate of 8% per annum.

7. Challenging the liability, this appeal has been preferred by the insurance company on the ground that tribunal committed gross error in holding the appellant liable for compensation referring to Naional Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Vimla Devi - 2014 ACJ 2072 in the light of the defence that offending vehicle was a freight carrier vehicle and can be only used for carrying goods.

entities.text: Naional Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Vimla Devi - 2014 ACJ 2072
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The insurance policy was issued for carrying goods and not for carrying passengers.
Accordingly, conditions of the insurance policy has been violated on the part of the owner of the vehicle.
He has referred to the FIR in which claimant himself has stated that he was going towards Jeerapur hat for buying buffaloes and after that he changed his statement for compensation.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:28904 3 MA-5654-2019 8.
Heard.
9. Counsel for the respondents have opposed the appeal and submitted that liability of the insurance company has been properly fastened after appreciating the evidence adduced on record.
10. Perused the record.
11. Tribunal has addressed the issue in para-15 of the award in which a finding is recorded that at the time of accident claimant was carrying buffaloes in the vehicle.
The finding of the tribunal is based on the statement of claimant (PW/1) and the driver of the vehicle Akbar Kha (DW/1).

The evidence of Pawan Kumar Agrawal (DW/2) is to the effect that investigator is appointed by the company but they have not brought on record the report of the investigating officer and due to this he is not in a position to state whether claimant was travelling in the vehilce along with the buffaloes or not.
In the light of this evidence, the finding of the tribunal does not call for interference.
This appeal is devoid of merit.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE hk/
